turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Siobhan Byrne? In you come, we'll do your checks before the doctor sees you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Grand, thanks. The M50 was a pure nightmare, we sat at the Red Cow for ages.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And your man in the jeep wouldn't let us in, beeping away.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I was fit to give out. Then the rain started, typical for a Tuesday.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is 132 over 78, pulse 84, temperature 36.6. The doctor's free now.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Lovely. I left the sample in the hatch, I'm scarlet carrying that yoke around.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): Siobhan, sit down. What can I do for you?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): It's the burning again when I pass water. Same carry-on as before.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): How many times this year?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): This is the third time this year. Well, actually, maybe the fourth, if I count the one after Christmas.
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She rang me in bits this morning. It's been going on nearly two weeks, doctor.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah Niamh, it has not. It came on last Saturday, so that's five days, not two weeks. You're thinking of March.
[SEG0013] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right, five days to a couple of weeks, we'll leave it. Burning every time you pass water?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, a fierce sting right at the end, and I'm going more often. Little and often.
[SEG0015] person_4 (DOCTOR): Up in the night?
[SEG0016] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Three times at least. She was wrecked with it.
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Not three. Once last night, and I slept after. I'm not wrecked at all.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the urine?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No, none that I've seen.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Pain in the loin, either side of the back?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing up there. It's low down, a bit of an ache over the bladder, that's all.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): Fever or shivers?
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She was shivery on the couch last night. I'd say she had a temperature.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): I was not shivery, and I haven't a temperature. I felt a small bit off, that's all, and cold from the rain.
[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any nausea or vomiting?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Appetite's grand, I had toast before we came.
[SEG0027] person_4 (DOCTOR): Vaginal discharge or itch?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that, God no.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any chance you could be pregnant?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No chance. My husband had the snip years back. He's on the metformin for his sugar, that's his worry, not mine.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): Your own tablets?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Eltroxin, a hundred micrograms, every morning, for the underactive thyroid. That's the only one I take regular.
[SEG0033] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And she took a few of my leftover trimethoprim. Don't be giving out.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): You took your sister's antibiotic?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): I did, I'm mortified. I took them for this burning. Two days, and then they were gone.
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): What strength, and how many a day?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): I'd say they were 200 milligrams. Maybe. One in the morning and one at night, I think. I'm not a hundred percent.

[SEG0038] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I can't remember if mine were the 100s or the 200s. I only take the biotin myself now, for the hair. The trimethoprim was from my own water infection in the spring.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): Allergies?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Penicillin. I come out in a rash all over. Years ago now.
[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any other medicines at all?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Niamh is forever at me to take biotin like herself, but I don't bother with it.
[SEG0043] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any leaking of urine, incontinence?
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I can hold it. I just need to go often.
[SEG0045] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'll examine your abdomen. Lie back.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Grand. While I'm down here, did you catch the hurling? My grandson got two points for the under-12s and we were soaked on the sideline.
[SEG0047] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's eight and he's already giving out to the referee. Mad for it.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): The forecast is worse for Sunday. We'll be drowned out in Tallaght.
[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): Abdomen is soft. Mild tenderness low down over the bladder. No loin tenderness on either side.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, that's the spot, just there.
[SEG0051] person_4 (DOCTOR): About the discharge. None at all?
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Well. Actually. There is a bit of an itch, and a small whitish discharge. I was too embarrassed the first time. It's not heavy.
[SEG0053] person_4 (DOCTOR): How long for the itch?
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, I'm not sure. A few days, maybe with this, maybe before. I can't put a date on it.
[SEG0055] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any smell from it?
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): No smell, no.
[SEG0057] person_4 (DOCTOR): This sounds like another urine infection. The itch could be thrush on top, I can't rule that out.
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): Thrush. I knew I should have kept my mouth shut.
[SEG0059] person_4 (DOCTOR): We'll send the urine off for culture.
[SEG0060] person_1 (NURSE): The dip is done already, doctor. Leucocytes and nitrites are both positive. I'll send the culture.
[SEG0061] person_4 (DOCTOR): Good. I'm starting you on nitrofurantoin for the infection, 100 milligrams twice a day for three days. Don't be taking anyone else's tablets again.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): Twice a day for three days, grand. Will that clash with the Eltroxin?
[SEG0063] person_4 (DOCTOR): Take the Eltroxin on an empty stomach as usual, and the antibiotic separate. Plenty of water. If you're not better in three days, come back.
[SEG0064] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And if the culture says it's the wrong tablet?
[SEG0065] person_4 (DOCTOR): The surgery will ring you if we need to change it. Otherwise carry on.
[SEG0066] person_2 (PATIENT): Do I need a swab for the itch?
[SEG0067] person_4 (DOCTOR): Not today. If the itch is still there after the antibiotic, we can look at thrush treatment then.
[SEG0068] person_2 (PATIENT): So I just finish the tablets and see.
[SEG0069] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes. Finish the three days even if you feel better sooner.
[SEG0070] person_2 (PATIENT): I will, I promise. Sorry for rambling, and for nicking the tablets.
[SEG0071] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): You're grand. I'll get her home. The M50 should have eased by now.
[SEG0072] person_1 (NURSE): I'll print the prescription and leave it at reception.
[SEG0073] person_2 (PATIENT): Thanks a million. Tell them at the desk I'll be a minute, I need the loo again already.
[SEG0074] person_4 (DOCTOR): On you go.

spec.situation: Woman with burning urine again; says 'third time this year' then corrects to 'maybe the fourth'; took leftover antibiotic from a sister; embarrassed; vaginal symptoms denied, then partly admitted. Urine test ordered.
features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.

bad.reason: Burning, severe sting, every time are supported; duration is disputed, not certain 'approximately 5 days to 2 weeks' by patient.

Negative finding missing: no vaginal itch was initially denied when first asked, before the patient later corrected herself to report some itch.
Negative finding missing: no fever was denied by the patient.
Negative finding missing: no shivers were denied by the patient.
Negative finding missing: no foul smell from the vaginal discharge.
History missing: this is the third time this year, or possibly the fourth if counting one after Christmas, indicating recurrent episodes/UTIs.
